You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

content = """ARC task-f2eb5109 VERIFIED NORMAL RULE: 30x30 background B, two singleton endpoints of path color P, and full horizontal bar rows with 3-cell portals of another color. Connect the top singleton to every portal center in top-to-bottom order and then to the bottom singleton, using P. From the current vertical column, draw down through the row immediately above the next portal; draw horizontally there to the next portal center; replace ONLY the portal center with P, preserving both side cells. After the last portal, continue vertically and draw the final horizontal segment on the bottom singleton's row. NO extra one-cell extension at either end for a normal large-displacement case.

TEST-VERIFIED ACCEPTED INSTANCE (zero-based coordinates): B=2, P=5, top=(1,24), bottom=(25,12); bars/portal centers=(7,6),(13,18),(18,10), base=4, portal sides=7. Accepted path: vertical c24 r1..6; horizontal r6 c6..24; portal center (7,6); vertical c6 r8..12; horizontal r12 c6..18; portal center (13,18); vertical c18 r14..17; horizontal r17 c10..18; portal center (18,10); vertical c10 r19..25; horizontal r25 c10..12. An otherwise identical variant with an extra P at (6,5), extending the first horizontal one cell left beyond the first portal center, was REJECTED. Thus prefer the exact inclusive endpoint ranges above and do not add the older memory's supposed top extension.

Historical anomaly remains separate: a different B=9/P=1 test rejected all rule-derived variants after 8 attempts. Do not let that anomaly change this now test-verified normal rule."""
res = rlm.harness.update_memory(id='arc_task_f2eb5109_verified_path_rule_and_anomalous_test', title='ARC task-f2eb5109 test-verified waypoint connector rule; no top extension', content=content, path='arc/task-f2eb5109', global_=True)
print(res)
